display_name: Bone marrow aspirate and core biopsy morphology
summary: Bone marrow aspirate and core biopsy (left posterior iliac crest) from a 58-year-old man with peripheral blood showing 41% circulating blasts. The marrow is markedly hypercellular (approximately 90-95%) with extensive replacement by immature mononuclear cells in sheets. The 500-cell aspirate differential gives 18% blasts, with promonocytes (4%) enumerated separately because their assignment is morphologically subjective. Blasts are medium-to-large with fine chromatin and one to three nucleoli; a subset shows folded or indented nuclei with grayish cytoplasm. No definite Auer rods are seen. MPO is positive in a minor subset of blasts (approximately 5-10%), and NSE is positive in a subset of cells with partial fluoride inhibition. The diagnosis is hypercellular marrow with acute myeloid leukemia, with probable monocytic differentiation to be confirmed by flow cytometry. The report states that the aspirate blast count is below the historical 20% threshold, that aspirate enumeration is likely affected by hemodilution and by difficulty separating promonocytes from blasts, and that classification depends on pending flow cytometry, cytogenetic, and molecular results.

stated_limitations: The manual aspirate blast percentage (18%) is below the historical 20% threshold. Aspirate enumeration is likely affected by hemodilution and by the difficulty of separating promonocytes from myeloid blasts on smears. Promonocyte assignment is morphologically subjective, and unequivocal promonocytes are difficult to distinguish from immature myeloid forms on morphology alone. Monocytic differentiation is probable only and is to be confirmed by flow cytometry. Classification depends on flow cytometry, cytogenetic, and molecular results that were pending at the time of the report. The report is a morphology component report that is part of a larger diagnostic episode and is not intended to stand alone.
